sources.name: U.S. EPA Envirofacts hourly UV index
sources.off_reason_was: 2026-10-25: the hourly UV service we called by LATITUDE/LONGITUDE now returns 404 (verified across gauges); the DAILY service works but is keyed by ZIP (getEnvirofactsUVDAILY/ZIP/<zip>/JSON), so a keyless lat/lon->ZIP step must be wired before UV returns. sources.name: Environment Agency real-time flood-monitoring API (Beta), England
sources.summary: API reference, read 2026-11-03: 'These APIs are provided as open data under the Open Government Licence with no requirement for registration. If you make use of this data please acknowledge this with the following attribution statement: this uses Environment Agency flood and river level data from the real-time data API (Beta)'. Every reply's meta.licence is OGL v3.0, whose text (nationalarchives.gov.uk, read 2026-11-03) allows exploiting the information 'commercially and non-commercially' with that attribution and a link to the licence. The reference also says the APIs 'should not be relied upon for safety critical applications' and asks for one readings?latest call per 15 min rather than crawling every station. Rainfall reference (/doc/rainfall, read 2026-11-03): same OGL terms, attribution 'this uses Environment Agency rainfall data from the real-time data API (Beta)', tipping bucket gauges, mm totals per 15 min; we read rain in one bulk call a run.
sources.credit: this uses Environment Agency flood and river level data from the real-time data API (Beta)
sources.evidence: curl of /doc/reference and /id/stations/4009 meta.licence 2026-11-03; OGL v3.0 page read the same night. Nothing from memory.

sources.name: Environment Agency Hydrology API, England
sources.summary: API reference, read 2026-11-03: 'All content is available under the Open Government Licence v3.0, except where otherwise stated'; every reply's meta says license OGL 3, publisher Environment Agency. OGL v3.0 allows commercial use with attribution. Readings carry quality (Good, Estimated, Suspect, Unchecked, Missing) and completeness flags; we keep complete days that are not Suspect or Missing. Soft limit 100,000 rows a call. Daily lowest and highest stage only: the API publishes no daily mean level.
sources.credit: Contains Environment Agency information licensed under the Open Government Licence v3.0
sources.evidence: curl 2026-11-03: /hydrology/id/stations.json?RLOIid=2102 (Colwick, wiskiID 4009, opened 1958) meta.license OGL 3; level-min-86400 and level-max-86400 readings 1964-12-30 to 2026-10-10, 22,571 rows; 15-minute level 2026-10-08 00:00 to 00:45 equal to the flood-monitoring stage 4009-level-stage-i-15_min-mASD to the mm (1.033, 1.037, 1.041, 1.041), so both are the same datum. Nothing from memory.

sources.name: Met Office Weather DataHub, Global Spot site-specific forecast (England pages)
sources.summary: DataHub FAQ, read 2026-11-03: products are made available 'under a perpetual, worldwide, non-exclusive, non-transferable licence to download, use, copy, publish, distribute, transmit, adapt and exploit' them in your application; users must include the attribution 'Powered by Met Office data'; commercial use: 'Yes. Subject to the terms of the licence granted to you.' Free plan: 360 calls a day, reset 00:00 UTC; we cap at 300 (collect.py MET_DAY). Owner subscribed and added the key as GitHub secret METOFFICE_SITE_KEY on 2026-11-03.
sources.credit: Powered by Met Office data
sources.evidence: curl 2026-11-03 of datahub.metoffice.gov.uk/support/faqs (licence, attribution, commercial use, 360 calls a day). Field names (screenTemperature, probOfPrecipitation, windSpeed10m, windDirectionFrom10m, dayMaxScreenTemperature, nightMinScreenTemperature) from WebSearch of user integrations, to be proven by the first live run's 'met ... fields' log line; a field not found is left out, never guessed.
